key_entities: git_adapter mutation primitives: add, commit, commit_tree, read_tree, rm_cached, update_ref, write_tree
propositions: The existing check_raw_git_writes.py gate (R1/R2) enforces mechanism (no raw subprocess git) but misses protocol violations (mutations outside atomic transaction) because it sanctions primitives at module granularity, allowing callers to compose them unsafely.

R3 (seam composition rule) must fire when a git-adapter mutation primitive is called from outside the sanctioned seam files (git_adapter.py, _ref_lock.py, _ref_lock_push.py, _pass_lock_lifecycle.py) to enforce that all tracker mutations route through atomic locked transactions.

R3 binds on receiver resolution (import bindings and dynamic-loader bindings per file) rather than bare names, so non-git-adapter .add()/.commit() calls (set.add, session.commit) do not trigger false positives.

Two durable reasoned inline markers are required at implementation: reconcile_helpers.py:226/246 (_commit_binding_store_snapshot) and __main__.py (_purge_committed_reconciler_locks in the relocated _pass_lock_lifecycle.py), both citing their specific boundary conditions rather than accepting debt baselines.

The gate lands after blocker tickets cubiform-wooden-fruitbat and gnatty-comparable-ynambu close, ensuring R3's first run enumerates zero unsanctioned out-of-transaction sites or only those with durable reasons, with no allowlist debt.
